subject: KMS operator heartbeat and rotor telemetry — review request
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Aamir Khan <aamir.khan@nebulahealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-14 09:12 -0700
Subject: KMS operator heartbeat and rotor telemetry — design review request

Hi Aamir / Priya,

Following up from our onboarding call — Nebula's SRE asked for more granularity around operator liveness signals and the rotation ("rotor") telemetry we surface for BYOK workflows. We've sketched a lightweight approach that avoids exposing key material while giving you clear indicators for: operator heartbeat, rotation start/complete, rotation failure with retry counts, and a mid-rotation pause (for manual escrow acceptance).

Attached: operator-heartbeat-spec.pdf (spec), kv-telemetry-sample.json (example payload), network-sentinel-diagram.png (edge layout).

High-level asks for this review:
- Do these signal names map to Nebula's on-call runbook?
- Is the suggested 30s heartbeat interval acceptable given your hop count and cross-region links?
- Any additional audit fields you require for compliance?

Marissa / Tessa — can you confirm the HSM-side events we can emit from the bridge without leaking entropy or key handles?

Thanks,
Diego

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: KMS operator heartbeat and rotor telemetry — design review request

On 2026-10-14 09:12, Diego Fernandez wrote:
> Following up from our onboarding call — Nebula's SRE asked for more granularity around operator liveness signals and the rotation ("rotor") telemetry we surface for BYOK workflows.
> Attached: operator-heartbeat-spec.pdf (spec), kv-telemetry-sample.json (example payload), network-sentinel-diagram.png (edge layout).

A quick note from the HSM/ops side:
- We can emit non-sensitive lifecycle events at the bridge boundary: rotation.start, rotation.stage(1|2), rotation.complete, rotation.rollback. None include key material or raw handles — only anonymized key IDs (hash).
- Heartbeat interval: 30s is fine for warm paths. For low-bandwidth air-gapped hops we recommend 60s with jitter to avoid synchronized spikes.
- We should include a monotonic nonce + signature verification field (signed by the bridge) so Nebula's sentinel can detect replayed/duplicated events if they ingest into a central SIEM.

I attached a short note to the spec highlighting the signature field and recommended jitter window.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: KMS operator heartbeat and rotor telemetry — design review request

Thanks Diego / Marissa — quick thumbs up from our side, a few clarifications: 

1) Jitter and 60s on air-gapped makes sense. We'll surface that in our runbook.
2) For the anonymized key ID, can you confirm the hashing algorithm and whether it is salted per-tenant? We need to map events back to our internal owner map.
3) Can the rotation.failure event include the HSM return code (not the stack trace) so we can triage immediately?

Also, related ask from our compliance reviewer — they want a documented way to replay the last two rotation events for post-mortem without revealing key material. Is that something you support?

Aamir
Lead SRE, NebulaHealth
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aamir Khan <aamir.khan@nebulahealth.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nebulahealth.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-16 16:44 -0700
Subject: Re: KMS operator heartbeat and rotor telemetry — design review request

Aamir — quick answers inline and a small proposal we can take to compliance: 

1) Anonymized key ID: we use a tenant-specific HMAC-SHA256 of the key ARN (or internal ID). The tenant HMAC key is stored in the bridge and rotated on our side; Nebula can supply a per-tenant salt if you prefer double-salting. We can add a mapping hint field (opaque id) in events that you can look up locally — it won't be shipped to Redwood's analytics.

2) rotation.failure: we will include an opaque numeric return code and a short categorical reason (e.g., TIMEOUT, ATTEST_FAIL, WAL_IO) but never any stack traces or raw error strings that could leak internal implementation details. That should be sufficient for triage.

3) Replay for post-mortem: yes — we can support a redacted replay API. Proposal: an authenticated endpoint that returns the last N rotation events for a tenant with all key IDs still anonymized and any sensitive fields removed. The endpoint will require a signed request from Nebula's tenant controller and will be rate-limited.

Action items:
- Diego: please update the spec to include HMAC-SHA256 + tenant salt option and the replay API stub.
- Marissa/Tessa: add a short note about the signed nonce and SIEM-friendly envelope.
- Aamir/Priya: confirm whether you want Nebula to manage the tenant salt or let the bridge generate one.

I'll draft the compliance blurb and link it to INF-4821.

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Staff Security Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
